page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 burstable virtual machine belonging to the shared instance family. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, providing 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. This instance configuration does not include local storage disks and provides zero discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage and maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect the architectural characteristics of the burstable CPU allocation and low memory density. Single-threaded metrics fall in the lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a single-core Geekbench score of 836.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1066.99, and weak single-threaded compression throughput. In contrast, parallel execution scales into average tiers, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 6235.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 16295.73. Memory throughput measures 99.9 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 57.76 GB/sec for writes, enabling standard multi-threaded throughput for operations such as Redis SET caching and static web delivery.

By delivering a high core count with a lean memory profile, ecs.t5-c1m1.4xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-parallel workloads that experience intermittent utilization rather than continuous peak load. The primary limitation is the burstable resource model, which restricts suitability for sustained full-capacity compute or memory-heavy databases. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, periodic batch processing, staging infrastructure, and horizontally distributed test runners.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.4xlarge is a burstable virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides an allocation of 1.0 GB of memory per core. The server contains no integrated local storage and no GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate weak single-thread performance, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 836.0 and single-threaded compression bottlenecks. Conversely, multi-threaded benchmarks reach average tiers, with a PassMark CPU score of 16295.73 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 6235.0. This burstable configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for intermittent, parallel workloads requiring high core concurrency. It is well-matched for distributed build jobs, low-traffic web serving, microservice staging, and bursty background batch tasks.
